findings.what: Existing same-session dispatch-ledger reader still treats a raw c.ok === true row as backing evidence for ping mode and never calls isVerifiedLivenessRecord/verifyRecord.
findings.why: testPing can stamp subprocess_verified from exit0 + envelope + an unsigned/forged dispatch-completions row. scripts/checks/liveness-read-choke-point.js scans only scripts/dispatch, scripts/checks, scripts/sprint, scripts/warpos, and scripts/events, so this scripts/ root reader is not caught.

findings.what: The structural guard is file-token based: any occurrence of isVerifiedLivenessRecord/filterVerifiedLiveness/verified-liveness-read/verifyRecord anywhere in the file suppresses all ok:true findings in that file.
findings.why: A new reader can import the helper but still gate on r.ok === true directly, or even mention verifyRecord in a comment, and the guard reports zero violations. The shipped test also blesses a file containing both isVerifiedLivenessRecord(r) and a separate somerec.ok === true expression. That is not a structural kill-the-seam guard.

parsed.summary: Focused direct-node tests for liveness-read, verified-liveness-read, role-resolver, gauntlet signing, coverage-gate, and panel-gate pass; node --test itself is blocked here by spawn EPERM. The ENV vector is closed in role-resolver: deriveBinding reads channel/role and the source guard confirms it does not read WARPOS_ACTOR_KIND or WARPOS_BOUND_ROLE as authority. The cross-session sealed-capsule ceiling was not re-raised. Verdict fails because not every same-session reader is verified and the guard can miss a newly added unverified reader.
